questions: How many nano-SQUID devices did you fabricate and cool down, and how many had working junctions with one or two working tunnel probes? You give the tunnel-probe yield as below 50% and show devices A, B and C; the totals would help.
Why were the others set aside? In particular, did any device with working junctions fail to show the Ic oscillations or the diode reversal (p. 4 says "all examined devices")?
Which ranges of field, field angle, back-gate voltage and temperature did you measure beyond the ones shown, and were the Bx sweeps in Figs. 1e, 3 and S2 also taken in the opposite sweep direction?
What does the second-best device or dataset look like: are there other single-probe devices like A, and did any show the abrupt zero-bias onset at half a flux quantum that Fig. 1f shows?

Could you compare Ic and eta versus flux, including how abrupt the reversal at Phi0(n + 1/2) is, with a trivial two-junction SQUID model built from your measured junction parameters, and say which feature of the global data that model could not produce?

Methods give tunnel-contact resistances "exceeding 100 kOhm", while the above-gap conductance in Fig. 1g and Fig. S2b is about 1 to 1.7 e^2/h (roughly 15 to 25 kOhm). What was each probe's resistance, and what filter resistance did you subtract, and how was it calibrated?

For the end-to-end correlation (Figs. 4c, f, i, l and S3), what threshold separates "correlated" from "no correlation", what bias step and smoothing go into the derivative, and how does Fig. 4l change when you vary them?

The Bx = 0 gate maps in Fig. 4a-b show resonances that cross zero bias. Did you look for Coulomb diamonds or even-odd patterns there, and at which field was Fig. S5 taken (its bias axes read in microvolts)?
